lines.label: Ayodhya, on the river Sarayu.
lines.text: Long ago, on the banks of the river Sarayu, stood Ayodhya, a city of gold and gardens.

lines.label: Four princes are born.
lines.text: Its king, Dasharatha, prayed for sons, and four were born: Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana and Shatrughna.

lines.label: The great bow of Shiva.
lines.text: In Mithila, King Janaka set a challenge. Whoever could string the great bow of Shiva would marry his daughter, Sita.

lines.label: Rama breaks the bow.
lines.text: Prince after prince failed. Then Rama lifted it, drew it, and the bow snapped in two. Rama and Sita were married.

lines.label: Two old promises.
lines.text: But back home, Queen Kaikeyi claimed two old promises from the king. Her son Bharata would rule, and Rama would live in the forest for fourteen years.

lines.label: Fourteen years in the forest.
lines.text: Rama left without a word of anger. Sita and his brother Lakshmana went with him.

lines.label: Sandals on the throne.
lines.text: Bharata refused the crown. He placed Rama's sandals on the throne, and waited.

lines.label: A golden deer.
lines.text: Deep in the Panchavati forest, a golden deer appeared. Sita longed for it, and Rama gave chase.

lines.label: It was a trap.
lines.text: But the deer was a demon in disguise, and the chase was a trap.

lines.label: Ravana of Lanka.
lines.text: Ravana, the ten-headed king of Lanka, seized Sita and carried her south in his flying chariot.

lines.label: Brave Jatayu.
lines.text: The old vulture Jatayu flew up to stop him, fought bravely, and fell.

lines.label: Hanuman and Sugriva.
lines.text: Searching for Sita, the brothers met Hanuman, and the vanara king Sugriva.

lines.label: An army of vanaras.
lines.text: Sugriva called his people, and a great army of vanaras gathered to help.

lines.label: One leap across the sea.
lines.text: Hanuman grew huge, and leapt across the ocean to Lanka.

lines.label: Rama's ring.
lines.text: In the Ashoka grove he found Sita, and gave her Rama's ring, so she would know help was coming.

lines.label: Lanka in flames.
lines.text: Caught by the guards, he let them set his tail alight, and leapt from roof to roof until Lanka burned.

lines.label: A bridge of floating stones.
lines.text: To reach Lanka, the army built a bridge across the sea, from stones that floated.

lines.label: Every stone says Rama.
lines.text: Each one carried Rama's name.

lines.label: The great war.
lines.text: The war was long and fierce.

lines.label: One arrow.
lines.text: At last, Rama loosed a single arrow, and Ravana fell.

lines.label: Home to Ayodhya.
lines.text: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana flew home to Ayodhya, in the flying chariot.

lines.label: A festival of lamps.
lines.text: The people lit rows and rows of lamps to light their way.

lines.label: Rama is crowned.
lines.text: And Rama was crowned king.
Those lamps are still lit every year, for a story of duty, love and courage. The Ramayana.
